title: Tencer 1982 lumbar joints (L2-L3, L4-L5): axial compression displacement vs force, intact, two groups of 5
condition: intact, no preload, nucleus pressurised to 626 kPa

quantity.name: axial displacement under compressive force (load-displacement curve)
quantity.definition: mean axial translation of the moving (upper) vertebra relative to the fixed one along the compression axis Z (through the disc centre) at each force step; force applied in 3 approximately equal steps to 823 N (1 min creep for steps 1-2, 2 min for step 3); mean of 5 joints per sequence

source.authors: Tencer AF, Ahmed AM, Burke DL
source.sample: two groups of 5 lumbar intervertebral joints (L2-3 and L4-5) used for the two sectioning sequences (Table 2), from 8 cadavers; disc grade 1-2

protocol.summary: Whole motion segments (posterior elements intact), lower vertebra fixed; nucleus pressurised to 626 kPa; 4 conditioning cycles of axial torsion; axial compression applied along the line through the vertebral body centres in 3 approximately equal force steps to 823 N; displacement read 1 min (steps 1-2) or 2 min (step 3) after each step. Force-controlled, quasi-static (creep included).
how_to_simulate: Model an L2-L3 or L4-L5 motion segment with posterior elements; fix the lower vertebra
Pressurise the nucleus to ~0.63 MPa if possible; no preload
Apply axial compression through the disc centre in steps of about 275, 535 and 823 N
Report the axial translation of the upper vertebra at each step (include creep for 1-2 min if the model is time dependent)
protocol.notes: Only the intact curves of Fig 5(g) and 5(h) are extracted (two sequences = two groups of 5 specimens; Table 2). Scatter bands at the middle step are not extracted: the caption calls them 'representative' and they cannot be assigned to one curve reliably.

extraction.check_notes: Axes calibrated from tick marks (182 px/mm, 0.456 px/N); marker centres from blob detection. Top step 824-825 N matches Table 3 (823 N). Middle step reads 531/540 N rather than 549 N (paper: 'approximately equal steps'). Consistent with the Table 4 mean flexibility f = 0.002 mm/N (1.31-1.64 mm at 823 N).

pass_rule.rule: model displacement within the range spanned by the two group curves (or +/-25%) at each force
